leads.summary: Related open shadow PR #13191 loses its outer card shadows when merged with the chamfer layer
leads.location: shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml:51-56 (PR #13191: shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml shadow Loader; shell/Ui/SurfaceShadow.qml padded source)
leads.consequence: On triangular themes with radius > 0, the card's layer captures only its own rectangle and its MultiEffect masks pixels outside the card outline. PR #13191 inserts SurfaceShadow as a child of that card, while the shadow is intentionally painted outside its bounds and its interior is masked out. The shadow on PopupCard, Clipboard, Emojis and Polkit cards will therefore disappear or be clipped if both PRs merge without placing the shadow outside the chamfered layer. Notifications' separate sibling shadow Loader does not share this problem.

leads.summary: Related open gradient fill PR #13120 leaves clear wedges on borderless chamfered cards
leads.location: shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml:38,51-56,74 (PR #13120: shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml gradient FillOverlay; shell/Ui/FillOverlay.qml outline)
leads.consequence: On a triangular theme with a gradient card and theme border-width:0, the combined card's native fill is transparent, and the new FillOverlay still draws a rounded rect with radius root.radius rather than the chamferSize cut or a square fill. The outer mask cannot add missing gradient pixels. For a 200x80 card at radius 20 and power 1, (x=15,y=0.1) lies inside the 10px chamfer (15.1>10) but outside the rounded 20px fill ((15-20)^2+(0.1-20)^2=421.01>400), leaving a clear wedge behind the diagonal. If both merge, square-fill under the mask or use a matching chamfer path; recheck any border overlay separately.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified FillOverlay.qml uses roundedRectPath at root.radius and BorderSurface color transparent in coord/pr-13120-files.json; point (15,0.1) arithmetic checked; Opus self-check CORRECT

leads.summary: Open PR #11951 implements the same rounding-power feature with an incompatible fifth geometry argument
leads.consequence: Both PRs change the same functions and add the same Hyprland getoption process under different Style properties. In #13166, geometry.borderPaths/ringPath/surfacePath fifth/fourth argument is a boolean chamfer; in #11951 it is a numeric rounding power and surfacePath expects numeric power. Blindly retaining either caller or callee during conflict resolution will map boolean true to numeric 1 or a nonzero power to true and produce wrong corners at powers other than 1 and 2. Their independently modified border-geometry tests also have incompatible literal paths. The merge requires a deliberate unified API and a single process, not a mechanical conflict selection.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified signatures borderPaths/ringPath/surfacePath(...,power) in coord/pr-11951-files.json; Opus self-check CORRECT

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Follow-up** to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13166#issuecomment-5823296938) of `cea8defa` and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13166#issuecomment-5825677960), checked at head `96c26ed6`.

**Verified:** the two new commits fix what the reply describes. The cut depth, the one-sided border spill, the four named highlights and the test gaps are resolved. Round controls keep their angular cuts, which the author states is intentional. No regression was found in the tested scope. The main remaining note concerns interactions with other open PRs that change the same component.

| Earlier point | Status at `96c26ed6` |
|---|---|
| Chamfer about twice as deep as Hyprland's window cut | Resolved |
| One-sided borders paint onto the borderless side | Resolved for zero-width sides |
| Round controls become octagons | Unchanged, intentional per the author and the PR description |
| Highlights left as plain `Rectangle`s | Resolved for the four named items |
| Test could not catch the geometry issues | Resolved |

**Verified** at `96c26ed6`:

- **Cut depth:** `chamferSize` now uses `radius * Style.cornerPower / 2`, which matches `CWindow::rounding()` in Hyprland 0.56.2. At `rounding_power = 1` the shell cut on large surfaces is 4, 6, 8 and 10 px for `decoration:rounding` 8, 12, 16 and 20, the same as the window content cut. The 30% cap now applies only to surfaces with a shorter side under about 33 px at rounding 20.
- **One-sided borders:** across 2,208 generated chamfer cases with at least one zero-width side, no paint lands on the straight part of a borderless side (2,130 cases did at `cea8defa`).
- **Rounded themes unchanged:** `borderPaths` and `ringPath` without chamfer match the base branch byte for byte in about 2.07 million generated cases, and `roundedRectPath` in 31,104. The converted Clipboard, Emoji, Tray and Polkit highlights render with the same corner geometry in rounded themes (qtdeclarative 6.11.2 clamps per-corner radii the same way as `radius`).
- **Tests:** `border-geometry-test.sh` passes on head (321 assertions). The same test fails on the `cea8defa` tree at the one-sided check, and fails on the cut-depth assertion when `cea8defa`'s `BorderSurface.qml` is swapped in. The pinned rounded literals equal base output. The clipboard, emojis, polkit and tray tests pass identically on base and head.

**Corrections to the earlier review:**

- The one-sided spill was described as a "~2.1 px strip down left and right edges". It was a small wedge next to the corner with legs of about 2.1 px, not a strip along the edge. The measured endpoints were correct.
- The coverage note was not exhaustive. Other plain `Rectangle`s with `cornerRadius` stay round on triangular themes, for example the weather location suggestion rows, the clock week heading and today cell, and the agents usage bars. Whether to convert them is a scope choice.

### Interactions with other open PRs

Several open PRs change `BorderSurface`. Three of them interact with this PR in ways that are not just textual conflicts. These results come from reading source; the combinations were not merged or rendered.

- **#13191 (shell shadows)**, when a theme enables shadows, adds a `SurfaceShadow` child to `BorderSurface` that draws outside the card's bounds. On triangular themes this PR enables a layer on the same item. A layer captures only the item's own rectangle (`qquickshadereffectsource.cpp`, default `sourceRect`), and the chamfer mask then cuts to the outline. So card shadows would be clipped away on triangular themes.
- **#13120 (gradient fills)**, when a theme enables a gradient fill, draws the gradient with `FillOverlay`, a rounded path at `root.radius`, and makes the native fill transparent. Under this PR's shallower chamfer mask, the area between the diagonal cut and the rounded fill would stay empty. For example, at radius 20 and power 1 the cut is 10 px, and point (15, 0.1) lies inside the cut outline but outside the 20 px rounded fill.
- **#11951 (rounding power)** implements the same Hyprland `rounding_power` support with a different API: the fifth argument of `borderPaths`/`ringPath` and the fourth of `surfacePath` is a numeric power there and a boolean here. Both PRs also add their own `decoration:rounding_power` query in `Style.qml`. A mechanical conflict resolution could pass a numeric power into this PR's boolean parameter; any power, including the rounded default of 2, is truthy, so every corner would be cut.

**Impact:** whichever of these lands after this PR, or before it, needs deliberate reconciliation. Otherwise shadows or gradient corners go missing on triangular themes, and the two rounding-power implementations can silently disagree.

**Suggested change:** mention the overlap in the PR description so maintainers can choose an order. For the shadow case, keep the shadow outside the masked layer (for example as a sibling) and give it the chamfer outline and cut size, since #13191's shadow and its cut-out mask use `root.radius`. For the gradient case, draw the fill square under the chamfer mask or with the chamfer outline.

**Remaining edge (predates the new commits):** when both adjoining widths are non-zero but unequal, the diagonal band is `(a + b) / 2` thick, so the thinner side widens past the corner: about 1.6 px for left 1 / top 3 and 3.7 px for left 1 / top 6. The taper applies only at exactly 0, so a 0.01 px side next to a 3 px side still widens by about 1.9 px. No default theme sets unequal per-side widths.

**Round controls at zero rounding:** the reply does not address the earlier sub-point that with `decoration:rounding = 0` Hyprland windows are square while controls with an explicit radius (slider thumb, Tailscale badge, and similar) keep their cuts. This remains a design choice for the author.

**Optional test improvement:** the cut-depth assertion pins only the text of the `chamferSize` declaration. Two mutations that point the chamfer mask or the border overlay back at the raw `root.radius` still pass `border-geometry-test.sh`, and would reintroduce the depth mismatch. Asserting that the mask and overlay consume `chamferSize` would catch that.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up review of commits `1c3cdde0` and `96c26ed6` against the earlier findings, read against Hyprland 0.56.2 (and `Window.cpp` from 0.50.0 through 0.56.1) and qtdeclarative 6.11.2 source. The geometry test, cross-tree and mutation runs, generated geometry comparisons and the clipboard, emojis, polkit and tray tests ran in an isolated sandbox with Node. Nothing was rendered: appearance, anti-aliasing, fractional-scale sharpness of the newly layered rows and the cost of creating a layer on each hover or selection change were not measured. The interactions with #13191, #13120 and #11951 were read from their diffs only. `./test/all` was not run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
